notes.title: Start here: Velocity Grid, an EOR platform under review
notes.body:
Velocity Grid is a multi-tenant employer-of-record app: Next.js App Router, Prisma and Postgres, with employees, payroll, tax rules, leave, contracts and billing. The `fable/` folder is a code review written against this exact snapshot; `docs/` holds the original author's feature write-ups.

Read in this order:

1. `fable/README.md`: the verdict and the "fix these first" list.
2. `fable/01-architecture.md`: the request path (routes, the `withRoute` wrapper, services, Prisma) and the auth model.
3. `fable/02-bugs-and-security.md`: one finding at a time. Each names a file and line, a fix and a general rule.
4. `docs/architecture.md`, the "Payroll engine" and "Events and worker" sections, for the tax maths and the outbox worker.

Keep `src/lib/api.js`, `src/lib/permissions.js` and `src/services/payroll.service.js` open while you read. The quizzes give a concrete request or input and ask what this code does with it.

excerpts.quote: Every claim below is tied to a real file and line and was checked by reading that code.

readMore.why: How a request flows and the patterns worth keeping.

notes.title: Two ways to reach the data, and who checks what
notes.body:
Data reaches a user by two paths. **Writes and API reads** go through `withRoute` in `src/lib/api.js`, which loads the session, checks a declared permission, validates the body and maps errors. **Page reads** are Server Components under `src/app/(app)/` that call `requirePageUser` and then a service directly.

For each quiz scenario, ask three questions and answer them from the code, not the docs:

- Which path is this request on, and what does that path check?
- Which permission does the route declare, and which roles hold it in `ROLE_PERMISSIONS`?
- Which identifiers does the service scope to the caller's organization with `resolveOrganizationId`, and which does it load with a bare `findUnique`?

Also read `loginWithPassword` in `src/services/auth.service.js` and list, in order, the checks it makes before issuing a session. Then read the user model's status values in `prisma/schema.prisma` and look for where each one is consulted.

notes.title: Money, the payroll engine and the event worker
notes.body:
Money is stored as `BigInt` minor units (cents). Read `src/lib/money.js` and note what each helper does with empty, non-numeric and fractional input.

The payroll engine in `src/services/payroll.service.js` has three steps: calculate, approve, process. For each step note what status it writes, what it checks first, and what it returns to the route. Then follow the return value back through `withRoute` to the HTTP response.

The tax maths is `computeTaxForRule` and its helpers near the top of the same file. Work one example per `calculationType` by hand, and read the `paidBy` branches at the end of the function.

Finally, `src/workers/domain-events-worker.cjs` drains the `DomainEvent` outbox. Read the `findMany` filter and the status written on success and on failure, and decide which rows a later run can see.

readMore.why: The payroll engine step by step, with line references.

notes.title: The page path never asks for a permission
notes.body:
`/payroll` is a Server Component that calls `requirePageUser()` and then the payroll service. `requirePageUser` only redirects anonymous users to `/login`; it checks no permission. `GET /api/payroll` goes through `withRoute`, which calls `requirePermission(user, "payroll.view")`. EMPLOYEE holds `leave.request`, `notifications.view` and `contracts.view` only, so the API answers 403 while the page renders every run (finding A0).

- *Both refused*: only the API path checks permissions.
- *Redirect to /login*: the user is logged in, so the redirect does not fire.
- *Both succeed*: the API does check, and EMPLOYEE lacks the permission.

notes.title: A permission name is not a scope
notes.body:
The PATCH route requires `tax_rules.manage`, which every CLIENT_ADMIN holds, and anyone can become a CLIENT_ADMIN by signing up. `TaxRule` has no `organizationId`, and `updateTaxRule` applies no tenant filter. Payroll calculation loads every active rule regardless of tenant, so the change reaches every tenant (finding A7).

- *403 for another organization*: there is no organization on a tax rule to compare with.
- *Only the new tenant affected*: rules are global, so there is nothing to limit the effect.
- *404 hidden rules*: the route serves any id to any holder of the permission.

notes.title: Committed first, serialised second
notes.body:
`calculatePayrollRun` commits its transaction (run set to PENDING_APPROVAL with totals) and returns the run row, whose totals are `BigInt`. Back in `withRoute`, `NextResponse.json` runs inside the `try`; `JSON.stringify` throws a TypeError on BigInt, the `catch` hands it to `toErrorResponse`, and the client gets a generic 500 (finding A1).

- *200 with strings*: nothing converts BigInt to strings on this path.
- *Rolled back*: the error happens after the transaction has committed.
- *Rounded dollars*: no rounding or conversion happens before serialisation.

excerpts.quote: return NextResponse.json({ ok: true, data: result });

notes.title: An id in a URL is not authorization
notes.body:
The payslip route is `withRoute({ permission: "payroll.view" }, ...)` and then builds `storage/payslips/<params.id>.pdf` straight from the URL. It never loads the PayrollItem, so it never learns which organization owns it and never calls `resolveOrganizationId`. If the file exists, it is streamed with status 200 (finding A2).

- *403 Tenant access denied*: that error comes from `resolveOrganizationId`, which this route never calls.
- *404 for another org's item*: 404 only happens when the file is missing.
- *401 owner required*: the caller is authenticated; no owner check exists.

notes.title: A status enum nothing branches on
notes.body:
`loginWithPassword` finds the user, refuses an unknown email with 401, refuses a future `lockedUntil` with 423, compares the bcrypt hash, and on success resets the counters and issues the session. `status` is never read, so a DISABLED user with the right password logs in (finding A4).

- *403 disabled*: there is no branch on status anywhere in login.
- *423*: that is the `lockedUntil` check, and lockedUntil is null here.
- *401 to hide the state*: 401 is only for an unknown email or a wrong password.

notes.title: Approve writes APPROVED without asking
notes.body:
`approvePayrollRun` loads the run, checks it exists, resolves the tenant, then in a transaction updates the run to `status: "APPROVED"` and its CALCULATED items to APPROVED. There is no check that the run is PENDING_APPROVAL, so a DRAFT run becomes APPROVED (with no items to approve) (finding A5).

- *409 for the wrong state*: that guard is the fix the review proposes; it is not in the code.
- *400 for no items*: the function never counts items before updating.
- *Calculates first*: approve never calls the calculate step.

notes.title: Only the room left under the cap is taxed
notes.body:
For WAGE_BASE_CAP, `computeTaxForRule` converts to major units, then `remaining = Math.max(0, capMajor - ytdMajor)` is 10,000 - 9,500 = 500, and `taxMajor = Math.min(taxableMajor, remaining) * rate` is min(2,000, 500) * 0.062 = 31. `toMinorUnits(31)` gives 3,100.

- *12,400* ignores the year-to-date amount and taxes the whole run.
- *0* would need YTD at or above the cap; $500 of room remains.
- *62,000* taxes the whole wage base, which is not this run's pay.

notes.title: The fall-through charges both sides in full
notes.body:
The end of `computeTaxForRule` has two explicit branches: EMPLOYEE returns the tax on the employee side and 0 for the employer; EMPLOYER does the reverse. Every other value, including the schema's third enum value BOTH, reaches the final `return`, which puts the full `taxMinor` on both sides.

- *2,500 each*: nothing divides the amount.
- *Employee only*: that is the EMPLOYEE branch, not BOTH.
- *0 for both*: BOTH is handled, by the fall-through.

notes.title: Silent zero on bad input, rounding on good
notes.body:
`toMinorUnits("abc")`: `Number.parseFloat` gives NaN, and the function returns `BigInt(0)` instead of failing (finding B5). `toMinorUnits("19.999")`: 19.999 * 100 is about 1999.9, and `Math.round` makes it 2000, so the result is `2000n`.

- *Throws for "abc"*: the NaN branch returns zero, it does not throw.
- *1999n after truncation*: the code rounds; it does not truncate.
- *NaN*: `BigInt` cannot hold NaN, and the guard returns 0 first.

notes.title: FAILED is a dead end
notes.body:
`runOnce` selects up to 50 events with `status: "PENDING"` and `availableAt <= now`. On an error it writes FAILED, or DEAD_LETTER when the attempt count reaches 10. A FAILED row never matches the PENDING filter again, so it is never retried and the 10-attempt branch can never be reached through retries (finding B9).

- *Retried, dead-lettered at 10*: that needs the select to include FAILED.
- *Backoff, then dropped*: there is no backoff code in the worker.
- *Retried because availableAt passed*: the status filter excludes it first.

notes.title: The lock is checked before the password
notes.body:
Each wrong password increments `failedLoginAttempts`; at 5 the update also sets `lockedUntil` to 15 minutes ahead. The next login checks `lockedUntil > now` before calling bcrypt, so it answers 423 "Account locked" even with the right password. The counters reset only on a successful login after the lock expires.

- *Successful login*: the lock check runs first and stops it.
- *401*: 401 is for an unknown email or a wrong password, and this password is right.
- *429 rate limiter*: the review notes there is no rate limiting at all.

excerpts.quote: const lockout = attempts >= 5 ? new Date(Date.now() + 15 * 60 * 1000) : null;

notes.title: A class-of-action permission with no object check
notes.body:
The sign route declares `permission: "contracts.view"`, which EMPLOYEE holds, and calls `signContract`. `signContract` never compares the caller with the contract's employee or contractor, so Jo signs Sam's contract and her signature is stored (finding A6).

- *Needs contracts.manage*: the route asks only for contracts.view.
- *Counterparty check*: that is the missing check the review asks for.
- *DRAFT only*: signContract does not check the previous status at all.
